lines.text: *An Act to extend the benefits of copyright to the nationals of nations which became combatants after June third, nineteen hundred and thirty-eight, by granting an extension of time for fulfillment of conditions and formalities. 55 Stat. 732, Ch. 421 (September 25, 1941)*

Be it enacted by the Senate and House of Representatives of the United States of America in Congress assembled, That whenever the President shall find that the authors, copyright owners, or proprietors of works first produced or published outside the United States of America, and subject to copyright or to renewal of copyright under the laws of the United States of America, including works subject to ad interim copyright, have been unable to comply with the conditions and formalities prescribed with respect to such works by the copyright laws of the United States of America, because of the disruption or suspension of facilities essential for such compliance, the President is authorized by proclamation to grant such extension of time as he may deem appropriate for the fulfilment of such conditions and formalities by authors, copyright owners, or proprietors who are citizens of or domiciled in the foreign state or nation affected, or who are nationals of a foreign state or nation which is party to a copyright convention or treaty to which the United States of America is also a party: Provided, That no extension of time shall be granted to any person (a) who has failed to comply with such conditions and formalities due to willful neglect; (b) who has engaged in or is engaging in the manufacture or sale within the United States of articles that infringe a copyright; or (c) whose government is not granting similar protections to citizens of the United States of America.

SEC. 2. That any extension of time granted by the President shall be effective as of the date specified in the proclamation and shall extend to the date specified therein, not to exceed one year after the termination of the existing emergency.
SEC. 3. That the President is hereby authorized and directed to prescribe such rules and regulations as may be necessary for carrying out the purposes of this Act.
